beliefs.practice: Always create and reuse a single MongoClient instance per process (or per container) instead of creating a new client per request; configure maxPoolSize to match expected concurrency (e.g., maxPoolSize=100) and set sensible timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS).

Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string/credentials out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (or individual creds) from environment variables and/or store them in Azure Key Vault and fetch at runtime rather than writing secrets to files.

Enable TLS/SSL for connections and validate server certificates (tls=true / ssl=true and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) to prevent MITM: ensure the driver connection string includes the required TLS parameters used by the cluster.

Grant least-privilege credentials: create a DB user/account with just the required roles (read on sales/lead_time collections, readWrite on purchase_orders) rather than using an admin/root credential in the app.

Model time-series-like sales velocity as one compact document per SKU (or per SKU+store) containing a bounded-size rolling window array or a summarized histogram rather than an unbounded transaction collection; if raw events are needed, store them separately and aggregate into summaries for forecasting queries.

Add a unique index (or unique field constraint) to enforce idempotency for purchase orders (for example unique compound index on product_id + period + supplier_id or a unique order_reference) and use upsert with that filter to avoid duplicate orders from the orchestrator agent.

Create TTL indexes for ephemeral agent memory documents (shared agent memory) to automatically expire them after the retention window (e.g., createIndex({last_updated:1}, {expireAfterSeconds: 86400})).

Index all fields used as filters or sort keys in production queries: at minimum index product_id, last_sale_date, supplier_id and any compound combinations used by the forecast or supplier selection queries to avoid collection scans.

For vector search, store fixed-length float32 arrays in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding: [f1, f2, ...]) and create a vector index specifying the correct dimension and metric (L2/cosine) so nearest-neighbor queries are efficient rather than doing an $where or application-side scan.

When creating a vector index, tune indexing parameters (index type such as hnsw or ivf, m and efConstruction for HNSW, nlists for IVF) and set ef (or efSearch) at query time to trade accuracy vs latency; persist these parameters as part of DB provisioning documentation.

Limit projection in queries to only the fields required by the agent (use find(..., projection={fields}) or aggregation $project) to reduce network transfer and deserialization costs when reading embeddings or large histories.

Use server-side aggregation pipelines (aggregation framework) to compute rollups and sales-velocity metrics instead of pulling large raw datasets into the app for forecasting; create indexes that support these pipeline stages (match->sort->group).

Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network and 5xx errors and limit total retry budget; use idempotent operations (e.g., upsert with unique key) so retries do not create duplicates.

Prefer causally consistent reads or explicit readConcern and writeConcern for workflows that require strong ordering (for example, make the orchestrator confirm a write is majority-committed before triggering supplier notifications); set readConcern='local' or 'majority' and writeConcern appropriately for required durability.

Provision collections with appropriate throughput/compute (provisioned RU/s or equivalent) and use autoscale if available; avoid saturating the DB with large bulk writes from concurrent agents—batch writes and use bulkWrite with ordered:false where idempotency permits.
When writing purchase orders, write small documents and store large static supplier metadata separately (supplier contact info, terms) referenced by ID to keep hot collections small and indexed.

Use change streams or a lightweight notification mechanism (if supported) to trigger re-evaluation by agents instead of frequent polling; if change streams are unavailable, schedule batched polling with backoff and lastProcessedTimestamp checkpoints.

Capture and log query performance: use explain() to verify that key queries (sales velocity aggregation, supplier selection, vector nearest-neighbor) use the intended indexes and avoid COLLSCAN; record and act on slow query alerts.

For latency-sensitive vector nearest-neighbor lookups, store a short pre-filter (e.g., category, product_type) and include it in the vector search query to reduce the candidate set and improve latency/accuracy.

Avoid server-side schema assumptions: validate inputs in the application (schema, embedding dimension, numeric ranges) and add JSON schema validation or triggers if the DB supports them to catch malformed documents early.
